In April 2025, the U.S. government, or USG, informed us that a license is required for exports of our H20 product into the China market. As a result of these new requirements, we incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 associated with H20 for excess inventory and purchase obligations, as the demand for H20 diminished

Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China's data center market that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government. We have effectively been foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market, and our effective foreclosure from the China market will help our competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge us worldwide

The availability of data centers, energy, and capital to support the buildout of NVIDIA AI infrastructure by our customers is crucial, and any shortage of these resources could impact our future revenue and financial performance. Expanding energy capacity to meet demand is a complex, multi-year process that involves significant regulatory, technical, and construction challenges

All of these factors may negatively impact our gross margins and financial results. We continue to increase our supply and capacity purchases with existing and new suppliers to support our demand projections and increasing complexity of our data center products. FULL.notes: [chunk 1/2] This extraction covers NVIDIA's Q3 FY2026 10-Q (filed 2025-11-19). Key SIFI-material findings: (1) Four direct customers represent 22%, 17%, 14%, and 12% of accounts receivable (~65% concentration in Q3 FY2026 vs. 2 customers at 17%+16%=33% in Q1 FY2026), indicating elevated customer concentration risk. (2) $3.6B in inventory provisions in the first nine months of FY2026 vs. $876M in FY2025 signals potential demand-supply misalignment or obsolescence risk relative to committed capex in manufacturing and cloud service agreements. (3) Anthropic PBC is named in a subsequent event context (dated 2025-11-19), indicating a recent investment or strategic commitment by NVIDIA. (4) The 10-Q references non-marketable equity securities investments (Note 6) but does not enumerate named investees in this excerpt; full Note 8 and Note 6 detail would typically show a roster of AI lab and compute company stakes. Unnamed customers A-D in compute segment suggest direct hyperscaler/CSP concentration but anonymity limits specificity for counterparty-web tracing. Manufacturing and cloud services capex commitments are disclosed as commitment items but lack specific dollar amounts, duration, or counterparty detail in this section.
